tells.1: Bolded label headers ('What you'll do:', 'What we're after:') over evenly balanced triads give it a polished template feel.
tells.2: none (clearly human but unskilled: all caps, missing spaces after commas, run-on sentences, 'preferrable' typo, boilerplate 'include but are not limited to')
tells.3: Inserted conversational fillers ('honestly, that's the fun part', 'your opinion will actually count') and choppy restated sentences read like a paraphrase pass over 1.
tells.4: none (mainly a factual slip: 'four-day week' conflicts with being open Wednesday through Sunday)
tells.5: Smooth, generic rhythm with the 'pressure cooker' line and tidy triads, but no concrete detail to anchor it.

reason: Version 4 is the only one with specifics a real kitchen would know: six cooks, about 180 covers on Friday, whole-animal butchery, the last sous staying four years, Luis moving up from dish, and fully covered health insurance. That makes it the most credible and human, though the 'four-day week' versus Wednesday–Sunday mismatch needs clarifying before it goes out. Version 2 is plainly human but too sloppy to publish.
